clue.text: By implication a badge bringing witty conversation

indicators.note: read as 'in-a', this phrase tells us to place the word in, followed by the single letter a, inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written, the word that is opened up
the 'im-plication' pun makes this single letter go in, so together with the inserting it stands for the pair of words 'in a'
the 'im-plication' pun makes this single letter go in, so together with the inserting it stands for the pair of words 'in a'

explanation.surface: A badge is said, by implication, to bring witty conversation with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By implication' is a pun: 'im-plication' puts IN and then A into BADGE, making BAD-INA-GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, teasing banter, a synonym for witty conversation.

clue.text: This shout is heard in dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A shout rings out at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bawl is a loud cry or yell.

clue.text: Infuriated when dull private gets out of step

explanation.surface: A sergeant is enraged when a dim soldier marches out of step.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means made extremely irritated or maddened.

clue.text: Symbol of rule man redesigned

explanation.surface: A man has redesigned the symbol of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a written symbol standing for a number.

clue.text: Kind and generous man of the 'our disappearing

explanation.surface: A kind, generous figure, the man of the moment, is fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'our signals a dropped H: man of the hour = HERO, so 'ERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a class or sort, so a kind.

clue.text: Bachelor attending quiet party

clue.text: Form of language in some respects non-U

explanation.surface: A kind of speech is judged rather unrefined.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper class; the joke is that this variety literally drops U from words such as colour and honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The variety spoken across the United States is a form of the language.

clue.text: Hindu festival head demonstrates religious quality

parts.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours
a ness is a headland

clue.text: English explorer revealing little bits and pieces

definitions.meaning: Matthew ..., the English navigator who charted Australia's coast

explanation.surface: An English explorer turns up small fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both that of the navigator and an old word for small fragments.

clue.text: Time locked in old chamber is eight days

parts.note: a cave is an underground chamber

explanation.definitionFit: In church usage an octave is the eight-day period of a feast.

clue.text: Poet and wife meeting murderer

clue.text: With hot drink to be imbibed call for splash of milk

clue.text: What agent offers is English gift — within permitted allowance

clue.text: Fight as expected by back of school

explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people.

clue.text: Common folk will have been pals, I suspect

clue.text: Quiet meadow certain to bring happiness

sure means certain

explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or delight, close to happiness.

clue.text: Nasty fuels spilt outside mine

clue.text: Parson set out to get female supporter

clue.text: Little child, girl, eating second pancake
